visual_comparison.subtitle: Five real locally archived Paspalum distichum photographs: rhizome/root masses, flowering V, actual membranous collar, spikelet-bearing rachis and wet-ground habit, plus separate Paspalum setaceum comparison. Same-plant rooted surface stolon, mature spikelet dissection and Pages QA remain unconfirmed.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: COUNT COMPLETE RACEMES → MEASURE 5 RIPE SPIKELETS → CHECK MARGINAL HAIRS → ROOTED BASE/COLLAR. DALLIS few large silky; VASEY many small silky; FLORIDA few big round; PUBIFLORUM smaller oval; SETACEUM narrow variable; DISTICHUM two + real stolons.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Paspalum: what to inspect
steps: Panel 1 (index 0): roots emerge from multiple nodes on a photographed underground creeping RHIZOME with attached shoot. This is clear evidence of real roots, NOT an aboveground rooting stolon at a visible soil line.
Panel 2 (index 1): count TWO attached one-sided racemes; panel 7 (index 6) is a DIFFERENT taxon (bahiagrass) with the same V, so head silhouette is not enough.
Panel 3 (index 2): point to the actual clear, short, projecting membranous inner ligule, not the sheath hair tuft; the image has no physical millimeter ruler.

NEW panel 8 (index 7) is another photo of the true free ligule (not the sheath-margin hairs): Harry Rose CC BY 2.0, original 1600×1200 sanitized. The translucent tongue is visible; no ruler exists in the picture, so do not count it as a measured 0.5–1.5 mm ligule.
Panel 4 (index 3): examine elliptic green spikelets on the rachis; none is dissected to confirm upper glume and different sterile/fertile lemmas at 1-mm scale.

Panel 6 (index 5) is habitat-scale wetland mat only. Find an actual live aboveground surface stolon touching soil and a definite emerging root at its node on a single documented Hays-area plant; photograph with cm bar and its flowering head.
Panel 5 (index 4) is another species, *P. setaceum*. Keep its old photo and photographer license attached; do not reuse its ligule or spikelet as if *P. distichum*.
Do not infer county-native presence from Australia; keep the existing BONAP county status unchanged and do not mark FINISHED without root-stolon and organ/site QA.

field_id_finish_pass.field_recognition: KNOTGRASS / WETLAND PASPALUM: often TWO narrow one-sided V-shaped flowering racemes, but that alone is not a species ID. It spreads in wet ground by surface STOLONS that root at nodes. The original photo proves the two-raceme V; the NEW licensed meadow photo shows low mat-like habit but does NOT prove individual rooted nodes. Separate from P. notatum (bahia grass) with a true runner and mature spikelet anatomy.

Bahia grass P. notatum also often makes two racemes; grass-root habit and mature upper-glume/spikelet measurements must corroborate. The Australian wetland image is not proof of Texas nativity.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: KNOTGRASS: find a low wet-ground perennial with real creeping aboveground stolons rooting at nodes, then usually TWO (occasionally 1 or 3) narrow, one-sided racemes making a V. Verify 2.4–4 mm mature plano-convex spikelets in two rows; the lower glume is absent or a tiny scale. Two racemes alone do NOT establish this species because bahiagrass also commonly has a V-shaped head.

measured_diagnostic_key.character: Stoloniferous, mat-forming perennial in damp soil; actual rooted nodes required, not inferred from a flat photo.
Usually 2, occasionally 1 or 3; about 2–8 cm long, one-sided spikelet rows; narrowly winged rachis.
measured_diagnostic_key.source: Flora of New Zealand; Kew GrassBase via AusGrass

measured_diagnostic_key.character: Usually about 2.4–4 mm long, solitary (rarely paired), plano-convex; one lower sterile and one upper fertile floret; no true long awns.
Usually absent or vestigial; if present a short hyaline scale, variable, not a long normal glume.
measured_diagnostic_key.source: USDA IDTools; Flora of New Zealand

measured_diagnostic_key.character: Approximately 2.6–3.6 mm, generally spikelet-length, usually 3–5 veins, finely appressed-hairy.
Approximately 2.6–3.6 mm, 3–5 veins, generally glabrous, not the hardened fertile grain cover.
Approximately 2.4–3.6 mm in AusGrass (2–3 mm in USDA IDTools); hardened, pale, awnless, often minutely hairy near tip.

Membranous, white; up to 1.6 mm in Florida treatment, 2–3 mm in Flora of China description. Different floras report different lengths; photograph actual inner blade–sheath junction with 1-mm scale. Hair tufts on sheath edge are NOT the ligule.

crew_sequence: Trace the stem to a visible root-bearing horizontal stolon node; distinguish stolon from an arching flowering culm.
Count complete attached one-sided racemes on one head; photograph the shared branch point.
At 10–20× measure five ripe spikelets and dissect a representative unit into upper glume, lower sterile lemma and hardened upper fertile lemma.
Expose inner ligule and adjacent collar with 1-mm scale; check sheath-margin hairs separately.
If rooting nodes or spikelets cannot be verified, record Paspalum sp. rather than species-certified P. distichum.

local_lookalikes.separation: Also frequently two racemes: do not identify from V shape; inspect rooted growth, rachis, spikelet shape and mature glumes.
Tufted or shortly rhizomatous, often paired smaller 1.4–2.6 mm spikelets and very short 0.2–0.5 mm membranous ligule; not a wet-ground long-stolon mat.
Usually a robust tuft with several racemes and conspicuously silky-margined larger spikelets; avoid raceme count as a sole character.

crew_separation: At wet margins, trace the low creeping horizontal stem before trusting its paired V-shaped flowerhead.
Look for actual roots on multiple rhizome nodes; in the field also follow a surface stolon, where it visibly roots and sends up shoots. The archived rhizome image is NOT the stolon photo.
Check the actual inner membranous ligule at the blade/sheath mouth. Existing photograph clearly shows membrane shape, but not millimeter length.
Check both closely spaced racemes and rows of elliptic spikelets. A two-pronged head ALONE is not enough to separate P. notatum.
Against P. notatum, inspect robust bahiagrass basal tufts/woody rhizomes and spikelet arrangement; do not decide from V heads alone.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — TWO RACEMES, THEN ROOTED RUNNERS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually two one-sided racemes forming a V; confirm a creeping stolon rooted at an actual node.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Begin with TWO full one-sided V-shaped racemes in gallery panel 2 (index 1). Check the wetland mat in panel 6 (index 5) and the actually rooted green RHIZOME in panel 1 (index 0): two separate nodes carry visible roots on a horizontal underground stem. This is NOT an aboveground stolon at the soil surface; that required photo is still missing. Bahiagrass at gallery panel 7 (index 6) ALSO has a convincing paired V, so never certify from raceme count alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL V-SHAPED HEAD + ROOTED RHIZOME — SURFACE STOLON STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · COLLAR AND TRUE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Expose the inner blade–sheath junction; published ligule lengths vary by flora.
field_id_short_tiles.details: TWO physically archived Harry Rose originals show the clear translucent true membranous ligule emerging from the inner blade/sheath mouth: gallery panels 3 and 8 (indices 2 and 7). The newly installed photo is a separate higher-resolution 1600x1200 angle (Flickr/Commons photo 8250242625), with an existing visual-only gross arrow to the actual membrane, NOT the sheath hairs. Both photos lack a physical mm ruler; 0.5–1.5 mm is the original photographer's stated range, not an independent measurement from these JPEGs. Other floras give different ranges, so confirm in the field.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TWO AUTHENTIC TRUE LIGULE MACROS ARCHIVED — PHYSICAL MM MEASUREMENT STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · RIPE SPIKELET ROWS AND REDUCED LOWER GLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Measure five mature flat-convex spikelets, generally about 2.4–4 mm long.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 4 (index 3) shows authentic aligned narrow green spikelets on a flowering raceme, distinct from one entire raceme. To confirm the 2.4–4 mm published range, photograph five mature spikelets with a 1-mm bar; lower glume may be reduced or absent and upper glume needs a real dissected view. No microscopic lemma/glume arrows are approved from the unscaled image.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · STERILE VERSUS FERTILE LEMMAS; NO LONG AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: One lower sterile floret and one upper fertile floret; hardened upper lemma is awnless.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The existing source-authenticated panel 4 (index 3) is a whole attached spikelet close-up, NOT a photo of the upper/lower lemmas separately. At 10–20× expose a lower sterile and hardened upper fertile floret, locate lower/upper glume and palea, and place a 1-mm ruler in the SAME plane. Dangling anthers and feathery stigmas in the head photo are not awns.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED REPRODUCTIVE KEY — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO DISSECTED FLORETS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES — BAHIA, THIN PASPALUM, DALLISGRASS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Never call knotgrass from the two-raceme V alone.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The final gallery panel 7 (index 6) is a REAL separately labelled *Paspalum notatum* head with the same V shape as panel 2 (index 1). Gallery panel 5 (index 4) is *Paspalum setaceum*, not knotgrass. To distinguish, physically trace the surface runners and roots, then compare mature spikelets and ligule. Panel 1 (index 0) only documents underground rhizome, not bahiagrass rootstock or knotgrass stolon. Dallisgrass also has a different, generally more robust many-raceme habit, but no matching Dallisgrass photo is displayed here.
field_id_short_tiles.status: BOTH BAHIA AND THIN PASPALUM PHOTO COMPARISONS COVERED — ROOTSTOCK COMPARISON OPEN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE — EXACT TWO-LANE HANDOFF
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — six own-species archived photographs, one local bahiagrass file, and one shared thin-paspalum photo.
field_id_short_tiles.details: EIGHT GALLERY PANELS: six same-species actual locally archived knotgrass JPEGs (rooted underground rhizome, V-shaped paired flowering head, TWO true ligule anatomical angles, elliptic attached spikelet closeup and wetland mat) plus other-species *P. setaceum* and *P. notatum* comparisons. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: a SAME verified Texas individual with true soil-surface aboveground STOLON visibly rooting at its node and attached full head, plus physical mm bar on one true ligule and a mature spikelet dissection (upper glume, lower sterile lemma, hardened upper fertile lemma). NEEDS_SITE_QA: photograph licenses, separate-source identifications, eight gallery panels, original annotation endpoints, live public Pages and mobile readability. Do not infer Hays BONAP from Australian photos.
